title: IDF Soldier Filmed Shooting Palestinian Man in Leg Near Faqoua, Jenin, Amid Settler Grazing Dispute
detail: On Saturday, September 12, 2026, an Israeli soldier was filmed shooting and wounding a Palestinian man in the leg on the outskirts of the village of Faqoua (Faqqua), near Jenin in the northern West Bank. Troops had been dispatched to the area following reports of a clash between Palestinian residents and Israeli settlers from the newly established Zayit Bagilboa farming outpost, whose livestock had been brought to graze on disputed land. Footage showed the soldier, standing alongside a group of settlers, aiming his rifle at Palestinian men in an agricultural field and opening fire on one of them, who was standing several meters away and not throwing stones or posing any apparent threat at the moment he was shot. The Palestinian Red Crescent transported the wounded man for treatment; his condition was not disclosed. The IDF said troops had fired shots in the air and then at a Palestinian after settlers came under stone-throwing, and confirmed an initial probe found the soldier violated the military's rules of engagement, with the case forwarded for review by the relevant authorities.

media.caption: Footage stills of the IDF soldier shooting a Palestinian man near Faqoua, Jenin, on September 12, 2026

confidenceReason: Corroborated by two Tier 2 Israeli outlets (Times of Israel, Haaretz) citing video footage and an IDF acknowledgment that the soldier violated rules of engagement, making the core facts of the shooting confirmed even though the IDF's characterization of the surrounding clash is its own account.

title: Pregnant Palestinian Woman Iman Shalouf, 27, Dies of Israeli Gunshot Wound in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis; Unborn Son Also Dies
detail: Iman Shalouf, 27, who was roughly seven months pregnant, died on Saturday, September 12, 2026 at Nasser Hospital from a gunshot wound to the head sustained days earlier while sitting inside her family's tent in the al-Rayyan/Tebbet al-Rayyan displacement camps near al-Mawasi, southwest of Khan Younis. Her mother-in-law, Wathfa Abu Mashi, said gunfire was heard from the direction of a nearby Israeli military position in the 'Yellow Zone' northwest of al-Mawasi before Shalouf was found bleeding from the head. Doctors initially detected her unborn child's heartbeat, but both mother and baby -- whom the family had named Ayoub -- died within hours. The Israel Defense Forces said it was looking into the incident. Her death came amid a Gaza Health Ministry report that 10 Palestinians were killed and 56 wounded in Israeli attacks over the preceding 48 hours.

media.caption: Coverage of the death of Iman Shalouf, a pregnant Palestinian woman shot by Israeli forces near al-Mawasi, Khan Younis

confidenceReason: Death, identity, and circumstances corroborated by both WAFA and Middle East Eye reporting citing family and medical sources; the IDF confirmed it was reviewing the incident but had not issued findings at time of writing.
